$comment: Dependency architecture policy for tools/quality/audit_dependencies.py. See doc/dev-notes/v2.4.0-requirements.md TASK 6 (gate G5). The rule is simple and deliberately strict: a library may depend only on libraries in a strictly lower layer. Same-layer edges are refused too, because they are how cycles start.

layers.name: core
layers.description: Numerics and transport primitives with no MNE-CPP dependencies of their own.

layers.name: support
layers.description: Cross-cutting helpers used by everything above.

layers.name: io
layers.description: File formats, machine learning back-ends and self-contained toolkits built directly on the primitives.

layers.name: model
layers.description: Domain models and format bridges assembled from the I/O layer.

layers.name: analysis
layers.description: Estimators that consume the forward solution.

layers.name: processing
layers.description: Signal processing pipelines that orchestrate the analysis layer.

layers.name: visualization3d
layers.description: Three-dimensional display, the top of the stack.

$variable_prefixes_comment: Variables that hold bare Qt module names; the namespace is prepended at the point of use with list(TRANSFORM), which the audit does not evaluate.
$allowed_external_comment: Third-party targets the libraries are permitted to link. Qt targets are normalised to a version-independent Qt:: spelling. Adding an entry here is an architectural decision and should be reviewed as one.

$exception_schema.$comment: Required shape of every entry in 'exceptions'. An exception is a dated promise: it must name the edge, an owner, a rationale, and an expiry date. Expired exceptions fail the audit, and exceptions for edges that no longer exist are reported as stale so they cannot accumulate.
$exception_schema.rationale: why the layering cannot be honoured yet
